evidence.contract: For repr(C) primitive products, generated hidden fast decoder checks padding, obtains byte slice, casts it to *const Self and calls ptr::read; comment asserts alignment 1.
Deserializer get_slice forwards to its reader.
BufReader promises byte slices and length, and &[u8] implements it by splitting at the cursor, with no Self-alignment guarantee.
Preserved local standard-library documentation states ptr::read requires pointer alignment; extract derived mechanically from retained HTML.

findings.reasoning: A paddingless repr(C) single u32 field has alignment greater than one on normal Rust targets. An arbitrary subslice can begin at an address not aligned for that struct; reading it with ptr::read violates the stated contract. Size equality does not prove pointer alignment. This is a source-level conditional, not an executed example or evidence of a production crash.
findings.conditions_and_limits: Requires actual expansion of a supported named repr(C) primitive product with align(Self)>1 and a call to generated deserialize_from_bsatn at an unaligned reader position. Generic SATS from_slice delegates to T::deserialize, not this hidden override (support/bsatn.rs 41–49); feature resolution, platform, callers and actual project ingress remain unproved. The inspected current basis-point structs have no repr(C).

lenses.assessment: Compiler symbols and schema field/variant names in lib.rs 114–166, sats.rs 54–80 and 492–505 are native grammar/identifiers; no application closed-string replacement established.

u8 sum tags and little-endian byte counts are native wire roles, not interchangeable product quantities. More than 256 variants and supported target/endian policy remain open; do not assert a cardinality bug without that contract.
SatsType owns compiler-side parse state; project basis-point numerical validity belongs to its own value type, while raw codec layout is upstream package ownership.
Current UnitBasisPoints and SignedUnitBasisPoints already own bounded numeric distinctions; conditional native field generation does not automatically call those owners’ constructors.
SatsTypeData Product and Sum select distinct generation shapes. Tuple-product unnamed fields and enum single-payload variants are separate cases and must not be conflated.
The native raw read path imposes alignment and byte-order conditions; current complement assumes an admitted basis-point range. No product fast-path execution or failure was observed.
Per-field codec validation cannot by itself enforce a whole-struct basis-point invariant; native layout size equality alone also does not establish pointer alignment or platform byte order.
The basis constructors reject out-of-range primitives, while the feature-gated generated native product directly constructs decoded fields. Actual feature selection and ingress remain unresolved.

Native enum AST accepts unit or one-field variants and rejects other arity; sum visitor recognizes tags/names and validates payload. This is not a blanket validation of all application enum invariants.

Schema type metadata, serialize and deserialize are generated together for SpacetimeType; compatibility between field representations and application admission remains a separate responsibility, not proof of duplicate authority by itself.

Any later owner change must preserve supported SATS schema names and tags, scalar little-endian wire semantics, optional feature gates, and intentional saturating vs fallible basis construction; compatibility shims are not requested.

Feature-gated project derive reaches the named 2.6.1 macro reexport at source level when enabled; producer/caller, feature unification, actual BSATN ingress and hidden fast-method dispatch have not been established.

SpacetimeType intentionally composes generated trait implementations; derive convenience alone is not proof that whole-value application invariants are enforced. No independent handwritten trait simplification is established.
